item.title: The AI Force the United States Needs is a Cyber Force
item.description: Cyberspace is the only warfighting domain without a dedicated service, and President Trump's calls for an AI Force won't fix that. A Cyber Force will.

item.title: Beyond the U.S.-China Binary: The New Landscape of AI Partnerships in the Global South
item.description: Global South countries are gaining new choices in building their AI ecosystems as China, India, and the Gulf States expand their technology offerings, creating new challenges for U.S. leadership.

item.title: Not Just an Island: Why Geography Should Not Drive U.S. Taiwan Policy
item.description: Taiwan’s geographic position in Asia’s first island chain should not become the main reason why the United States supports Taiwan’s security. The main focus of U.S. policy should be preventing a PRC attack on Taiwan and the regional and global catastrophe it would cause.

item.description: This edition of States Weekly covers October 21, 2026.

item.title: Human Rights Initiative Director's Note: October 2026 Edition
item.description: The October 2026 edition of the Human Rights Initiative Director's Note where Andrew Friedman shares his reflections on human rights and democracy issues occupying significant space in his mind, highlights key HRI ongoings, and spotlights notable articles and videos he's come across.

item.title: Cartels, Cameras, and Commercial Data: Nonstate Actors and Ubiquitous Technical Surveillance
item.description: The most advanced nation-states can exploit ubiquitous technology, data, and connectivity to advance intelligence and military aims—but now, cartels and violent criminal organizations can too.

item.title: Why the United States Needs Europe in Order to Win the Technology Race
item.description: Europe is both a vast market and a coproducer of U.S. technology. To outcompete China, the United States must offer allies a stake in building the future rather than exploit their dependencies.
